summary: The root لهب (lhb) primarily describes fire flaming or blazing, especially without smoke. It also refers to lightning flashing continuously.
lane: 4 الهب النَّارَ ذ He made the fire to flame, or blaze: (S:) or made it to flame, or blaze, free from smoke. (K.) -b2- الهب It (lightning) flashed uninterruptedly. (K.) See also أَهْلَبَ . -b3- الهب , inf. n. إِلْهَابٌ , He (a horse, As, or other thing that runs, Lh,) was ardent, or impetuous, in his course, or running; (As, S;) as also اهلب : (As:) or he ran with energy, or effort, so as to raise the dust: (K:) or he ran violently, raising the لَهَبَ , or dust. (TA.) -b4- Hence, الهب فِى الكَلَامِ (tropical:) He spoke rapidly [ and with vehemence ]. (TA.) -b5- الهبهُ الأَمْرُ (tropical:) The thing, or affair, excited him, and inflamed him. (TA.)

headwords.def: لَهِبَ, aor. لَهَبَ, (inf. n. لَهَبٌ, S,) (tropical:) He thirsted; was thirsty: (S, K:) [probably, burned with thirst ].

لهّب النَّارَ [same as, except that it has an intensive signification; He made the fire to flame, or blaze, fiercely, or intensely: or, to flame, or blaze, without smoke, fiercely, or intensely. ] (K.)

الهب النَّارَ He made the fire to flame, or blaze: (S:) or made it to flame, or blaze, free from smoke. (K.) الهب It (lightning) flashed uninterruptedly. (K.) See also أَهْلَبَ. الهب, inf. n. إِلْهَابٌ, He (a horse, As, or other thing that runs, Lh,) was ardent, or impetuous, in his course, or running; (As, S;) as also اهلب: (As:) or he ran with energy, or effort, so as to raise the dust: (K:) or he ran violently, raising the لَهَبَ, or dust.

تلهّبت النَّارُ, quasi-pass. of لَهَّبَ, (K,) [same as, except that it has an intensive signification;] The fire flamed, or blazed, (S,) [ fiercely, or intensely, or flamed, or blazed, burned without smoke, fiercely, or intensely ]. تلهّب جُوعًا, and جوعا, (tropical:) He burned with hunger. (TA.) تلهّب غَيْظًا He burned, and was or became hot, with wrath, or rage. (TA, art. وغر.) See 8.

التهبت النَّارُ, quasi-pass. of أَلْهَبَ, (K,) The fire flamed, or blazed: (S:) or flamed, or blazed, free from smoke. (K.) التهب عَلَيْهِ (tropical:) He was incensed, or inflamed with anger, against him. (TA.) التهب and [ It (any part of the body) became inflamed ]. See 5.

لِهْبٌ A gap, or space, between two mountains: (S, K:) or a cleft, or fissure, in a mountain: (Lh, K:) or a small gap, or ravine, such as is termed شِعْبٌ, in a mountain: (K:) or a cleft in a mountain, afterwards widening like a road: a لِصْب and a شَقّ are smaller than a لهب; like a small road: (Aboo-Sa'eed-Es-Sukkaree:) or a face of a mountain, resembling a wall, that cannot be ascended: (K:) and similar to this is the لهب of the sky at the horizon: or, as some say, a subterranean excavation,…

لَهَبٌ and (K) and and and (S, K), [inf. ns., of which the verb, لَهِبَ, aor. لَهَبَ, does not appear to have been used in the classical ages,] The flaming, or blazing, of fire: (S:) or its flaming, or blazing, free from smoke: (T, K:) or لَهَبٌ signifies the flame, or blaze, of fire: (S, K:) and, its heat. (K.) لَهَبٌ Dust rising (K) like smoke. (TA.)

لُهْبَةٌ A clear white colour: (K:) brightness of the complexion, or colour of the skin. (TA.) لُهْبَةٌ (in two copies of the S, لَهْبَةٌ; but in the K expressly said to be with dammeh;) and and (K) (tropical:) Thirst: (S, K:) [probably burning thirst ].

لَهَبَانٌ: see لَهَبٌ and لُهْبَةٌ. Also, The burning of coals, or embers, without blazing. (T.) The burning of heat upon heated ground. (TA.) Vehemence of heat (K) upon heated ground and the like. (ISd.) A hot day. (K.)
لَهْبَانُ, fem. لَهْبَى, (tropical:) Thirsty: (S, K:) [probably burning with thirst: ] an epithet applied to a man or woman: (S:) pl. لِهَابٌ. (K.)
لُهَابَةٌ A garment ( كِسَاءٌ ) in which a stone is put, and with which one side of the kind of camel-litter called هَوْدَج, or one side of a load, is balanced. (Th.)

أُلْهُوبٌ, a subst., The ardour, or impetuosity, of a horse ( &c., Lh) in his course, or running: (S:) or his energy, or effort, in his course, so that he raises the dust: or a violent run, by which the dust ( اللَّهَبُ ) is raised: (TA:) or the commencement of a horse's course, or run. (K.) لَهُ أُلْهُوبٌ He runs violently, raising the dust. (TA.) See also أُهْلُوبٌ. Also used as an epithet: you say شَدٌّ أُلْهُوبٌ [ A violent run, in which the dust is raised ]. (TA.)
مِلْهَبٌ Pleasing in beauty: (IAar, K:) and having much hair: an epithet applied to a man. (IAar.)
مُلَهَّبٌ (tropical:) A garment, or piece of cloth, not saturated with red dye: (K:) imperfectly dyed. (TA.)

headword_note: Lane indexes geminate roots with two letters where the Corpus uses three; both spellings are resolved here.
mentions_note: Forms Lane discusses inside another entry rather than defining as a headword. Values index into headwords[].
